open.speaker: r62_farmer
lines: Come in off the road, you'll get hit. Nobody drives 62 slow since the county fixed it.
Whitmore. Ab. You're from Sutton, Marlene said. Kettle's on, dog's bowl is full and there's no dog, so you may as well talk.
He said the dog before the kettle, dear.

passives.line: The bowl's on the porch, full, with frost on the water. He fills it every morning and doesn't tip it out.
There's a scuff in the snow at the barn's peak. Not a ladder mark. Something set down there.
The county notice is on the dresser through the window. He keeps paperwork. There's none for the dog.

options.text: Twenty-two feet. What on this farm reaches twenty-two feet?

fail.line: Ladder. Wind. A dog can climb a thing when he's scared enough. I've thought of all of it, and I'll thank you not to.

options.text: Nothing on this road's a monster, is it, Ab.

boone.speaker: r62_farmer
lines: Boone. Eleven, bluetick, deaf in one ear. Went out Monday barking at the barn and didn't come back.
Thirty-one years of dogs. They come back. They come back hurt, they come back ashamed, they come back.
He's still listening for him. Under everything you say.

twentytwo.speaker: r62_farmer
lines: Nothing. Hay elevator's sixteen and it's been broke since fall. I measured, 'cause I'm that kind of fool.
Collar was buckled. Not torn. Buckled, and set on the ridge like you'd set down a hat.
Set down. Not dropped. Something with hands, or something careful.

nothing.speaker: r62_farmer
lines: No. The culvert's the county, the owls are owls, and half this road's seen a barn owl in the headlights and called the Register.
...The collar I don't have a thing for. I've tried.
A natural column with one row empty. I'll take it. I'll take it honestly.

hub.speaker: r62_farmer
lines: Kettle's on. Ask what you came to ask.

static.line: The collar's on the dresser with the county notice. He's filed it with the paperwork. Ask him what he thinks it proves.

options.text: An owl screams like a woman. What would your grandmother have said about Monday?
You still fill his bowl, Ab. What did you hear Monday that you haven't said?
A black sedan sat at the chapel Monday and Tuesday. You'd have seen it.

grandmother.speaker: r62_farmer
lines: She'd have said it's a bad road. Said it in '31 when they built the chapel, said it when they closed it.
Called the TNT ground 'the bird's field' before there was a plant. Everybody's granny did. Nobody asked why.

grandmother_fail.speaker: r62_farmer
lines: She'd have said mind your business and come in out of the cold. So would I.
Owls are owls. Go look in the steeple if you don't believe me. Bring a hat.

heard.speaker: r62_farmer
lines: ...It wasn't a scream. Owls scream. Boone yelped once, the way he did as a pup when I stepped on him.
Then quiet. Not quiet like the night. Quiet like a room with the door shut. And the barn roof creaked once, the way it does under a man.
I didn't go out. Thirty-one years, and I didn't go out for my dog.
He thinks that's the thing he'll answer for. It isn't. Tell him it isn't.

heard_fail.speaker: r62_farmer
lines: You want to hear things in the night, Carl Ridge sits up a tree and hears plenty. Go sit with Carl.

sedan.speaker: r62_farmer
lines: Saw 'em. Two nights. I thought county at first, then state, then I stopped thinking.
Tuesday one of 'em got out and walked up my lane and stood by the barn and looked up. Just looked up. Then got back in.
He wasn't looking at the roof. He was looking where the roof would be if the barn weren't there.
He knew the height. Before the collar was found.

bowl.speaker: r62_farmer
lines: (He watches you do it. He doesn't stop you.)
...Thank you. Thirty-one years, nobody's done that but me.
